children: TOKYO, November 19 (Reuters) - Foreign investors remained netsellers of Japanese stocks for the week ending on November 14, capital flows data showed on Thursday.    Foreigners sold a net 224.1 billion yen worth of shares inthe week through Nov. 14, after selling a net 102.3 billion yenin the week before that.    Japanese investors sold a net 440.7 billion yen of foreignbonds in the latest week after selling a net 534.1 billion yenthe week before.    Details of net investments were as follows (in billion yen):

FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN JAPAN:    (net)                                       stocks         bonds        bills    November 8  - November 14          -224.1        +650.1       +161.8     November 1  - November 7           -102.3r     +1,370.9r    -1,513.2r
JAPANESE INVESTMENT ABROAD:    (net; a minus sign indicates net selling and inflows of funds into Japan)
stocks         bonds        bills    November 8  - November 14          +363.1        -440.7       +190.8     November 1  - November 7           -658.2r       -534.1r       +66.3

Notes:    - An "r" denotes a revised figure.    - Bonds include beneficiary certificates.    - Figures are based on contracts and are rounded.    - The MOF's capital flows data can be found in English at:    http://www.mof.go.jp/international_policy/reference/itn_transactions_in_securities/week.pdf
